Principle 03 of 8

Privacy

Collect only what is needed, use it only as agreed, and protect it.

Protects

Customers, workers, people who never signed up

Why it matters

Personal information outlives the moment it is given, and it can be used against the person it describes.

Covers

Data collection, tracking, retention, sale, and breach handling (Category 4), and consent to data use (5.1).

3.5 Forced Action · 5 practices

Privacy+ Autonomy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
3.5.1Forced RegistrationRequiring account creation for actions that don't need persistent identity (viewing prices, completing a one-time purchase).E-commerce, news/media, software downloads
3.5.2Forced ContinuityAutomatic conversion of a free trial to paid without a clear pre-charge prompt.Streaming, supplements, software
3.5.3Friend Spam / Contact UploadRequiring contact-list access or social-graph permissions as a condition of basic functionality.Social media, productivity apps
3.5.4Forced Ad TargetingMaking personalized ad targeting a non-negotiable condition of using the service, even in paid tiers.Social media, streaming
3.5.5Aggressive In-Person SolicitationVerbal solicitation, shouting, harassment, or physical blocking of potential customers in transit hubs and tourist zones to coerce a transaction before they can compare alternatives.Taxi services at airports/stations, timeshare reps, street vendors

4.1 Over-Collection · 5 practices

Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.1.1Excessive Data CollectionGathering more data than is necessary for the stated purpose.Cross-domain (mobile apps, automotive infotainment, smart appliances, fitness, gaming)
4.1.2Purpose CreepUsing data collected for one purpose ("service improvement") for unrelated purposes (ad targeting, employee evaluation, partner deals) without renewed consent.Internal company ethics, social media, telecom, healthcare
4.1.3Cloud-Dependency CoercionRequiring cloud connectivity for core product functionality so data collection becomes a precondition of operation.Home appliances, automotive, gaming
4.1.4Phoning Home Without PurposeSoftware transmitting telemetry to company servers when no cloud feature is needed for the product to function.Operating systems, productivity software, smart appliances
4.1.5Infotainment / Synced-Phone HarvestingCollecting contacts, calendar entries, text messages, or media from a connected phone without clear disclosure.Automotive infotainment, smart TVs

4.2 Shadow Profiling of Non-Users · 3 practices

Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.2.1Shadow ProfilingBuilding behavioral, demographic, or social-graph profiles of individuals who have never created accounts, via pixels, contact uploads, or third-party data.Social media, advertising, data brokers, internal company ethics
4.2.2Public-Records Aggregation ProfilingCombining disparate public records — court filings, deeds, voter rolls — into invasive composite profiles.Data brokers, credit reporting
4.2.3Inferred-Attribute ProfilingUsing algorithms to infer protected or sensitive characteristics (health conditions, sexuality, religion, immigration status) from behavioral data.Data brokers, advertising, insurance

4.3 Cross-Device & Cross-Platform Tracking · 5 practices

Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.3.1Cross-Site Tracking Without ConsentFollowing users across sites and apps via tracking pixels, device graphs, or identifier sharing.Digital advertising, social media
4.3.2Browser & Canvas FingerprintingUsing browser, canvas, or device fingerprinting to circumvent cookie restrictions and re-identify users who have cleared cookies.Digital advertising
4.3.3Cross-Device Identity StitchingLinking activity across a user's phone, tablet, and desktop into unified profiles without explicit consent.Digital advertising, search engines
4.3.4Cross-Product Data FusionMerging data across multiple products of the same vendor into unified profiles without product-specific consent.Internal company ethics, large platforms
4.3.5Cross-Service Data SharingUsing customer data from one service to benefit another service in the provider's portfolio without explicit consent.Cloud/SaaS, streaming, telecom

Privacy+ Responsibility
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.6.1Keystroke / Screen MonitoringRecording keystrokes, screenshots, or screen contents continuously or at random intervals without meaningful notice.Internal company ethics, surveillance technology, staffing/temp agencies

4.6.3Productivity Score QuantificationAssigning numerical scores based on mouse movement, idle time, or app switching, then using them in performance, termination, or promotion decisions.Internal company ethics, surveillance technology

4.6.5Personal-Device MDM IntrusionRequiring monitoring or MDM software on personally owned devices as a condition of employment.Internal company ethics
4.6.6Union-Busting SurveillanceTools or services designed to identify, track, or undermine labor organizing.Surveillance technology
4.6.7AI-Driven Worker MonitoringTracking keystrokes, bathroom breaks, movement, or productivity to create constant surveillance environments.AI vendors, warehousing, call centers, ride-hailing, food delivery

Privacy+ Fairness
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

4.12 Breach Notification Failures · 4 practices

Privacy+ Accountability
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.12.1Breach Notification DelayDelaying disclosure of data breaches beyond legally required timelines to manage PR or assess liability.Cross-domain (financial services, cloud, credit reporting, telecom, data brokers, retail)
4.12.2Breach Severity DownplayingMinimizing the scope, data types, or number of affected individuals in public disclosures, providing technically accurate but materially misleading statements.Cybersecurity, healthcare
4.12.3Breach Insurance UpsellingUsing a breach event as an opportunity to sell identity-theft monitoring rather than improving baseline security.Credit reporting, financial services
4.12.4Breach-Insurance Vacuum for AffectedCarrying no provision or insurance to compensate data subjects harmed by breaches, leaving victims without recourse.Data brokers

5.1 Consent Manipulation · 7 practices

Privacy+ Autonomy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
5.1.1Bundled ConsentRequiring users to accept broad data collection, tracking, and analytics as a single all-or-nothing package rather than granular choices.Internal company ethics, social media, mobile apps
5.1.2Coerced Consent"Accept or leave" ultimatums that make refusal impractical even when refusal should be a viable option.Social media, telecom, healthcare (data sharing in treatment forms)
5.1.3Consent FatigueOverwhelming users with repeated or fragmented consent requests so that meaningful choice degrades into reflexive acceptance.Cookie banners, mobile permissions
5.1.4Opt-Out Friction / BurialBurying tracking opt-outs in obscure settings, requiring admin privileges, resetting preferences after updates, or requiring account creation to opt out.Internal company ethics, advertising, social media
5.1.5Opt-Out ExpirationSetting time limits on opt-out requests, automatically re-enrolling consumers in data collection after a period.Data brokers
5.1.6Coerced Wearable / Telematics SharingConditioning meaningful discounts on sharing of wearable, driving, or other behavioral data, penalizing privacy-conscious customers.Insurance, automotive
5.1.7Genetic Data CoercionUsing or requesting genetic testing data for underwriting decisions or as a condition of service.Insurance

5.3 Misleading Privacy Claims · 4 practices

Privacy+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
5.3.1Deceptive De-Identification ClaimsClaiming telemetry or shared data is "anonymous," "aggregated," or "crash-only" when it is sufficient to identify or re-identify individuals.Internal company ethics, healthcare
5.3.2Re-Identifiable Anonymized SharingSharing supposedly anonymized datasets that can be cross-referenced to re-identify subjects.Prison/corrections, healthcare
5.3.3Selective Transparency ReportingPublishing transparency or data-request reports that omit proprietary surveillance, internal monitoring, or shadow profiling volumes.Internal company ethics, social media
5.3.4Security-Veiled SurveillanceJustifying invasive tracking under the pretense of "security," "fraud prevention," or "integrity" when the primary use is behavioral analytics.Internal company ethics, financial services
